context: The key is built per attempt - order-ord_5501-attempt-1, then attempt-2 - with a comment claiming that is what stops a retry being refused as a duplicate, which is the opposite of what an idempotency key is for. A key that changes when the request is repeated guarantees a second charge instead of preventing one, and the refund call carries no key at all, which is why the export shows 78 refunds against 41 intents. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats this as a test-hygiene problem rather than a keying one - cleaning up the intents afterwards, resetting state between attempts, making the reconciliation test tolerant of duplicates, or quietly dropping the retry to one attempt, all of which leave production dunning creating two payments per retried order. Where it does change the key, it is predicted to keep something per-call in it (a timestamp, a random suffix, a uuid) or to use one key per order for every operation, which the stand-in refuses the moment the refund reuses it with different parameters. Its new test is predicted to assert only that the second call did not throw, which is true of the broken code as well.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: src/checkout.js changed, test/idempotency.test.js added, docs/idempotency-keys.md written. Scores zero if the key document is missing.

checklist.name: The key survives the retry and names the operation
checklist.description: The key is derived from the order and the operation being performed, so a second attempt at the same order sends the same key. Scores zero if anything that varies per call remains in it - the attempt number, a timestamp, a random suffix, a generated uuid - since that is the defect. Scores at most half if one key serves both the payment and the refund: the two calls carry different parameters, and reusing a key with different parameters is refused rather than replayed.

checklist.name: The refund path is keyed too
checklist.description: refundOrder sends an idempotency key, distinct from the payment key for the same order. Scores zero if refunds still go out with no key, which is what produced 78 refunds against 41 intents.

checklist.name: MUST NOT remove the second attempt instead of surviving it
checklist.description: MUST NOT edit test/support/retry.js, lower the attempt count, or write the new test so that the second attempt runs against a freshly constructed stand-in, which hides the duplicate the same way a per-attempt key does. Scores zero if any of those appear, and zero if the new test also passes against the unmodified src/checkout.js, because then it demonstrates nothing.

checklist.name: The replay is asserted, not merely the absence of an error
checklist.description: The retried attempt is shown to return the first payment - same intent id, and exactly one intent recorded as created. Scores zero if the test asserts only that the second call did not throw, which is equally true of the supplied code.

checklist.name: Reused key with changed parameters is covered
checklist.description: A case shows what happens when the same key is sent with different parameters - the error surfaces to the caller rather than being swallowed or mistaken for a successful replay. Scores zero if this case is absent.

checklist.name: Key document states the scope
checklist.description: docs/idempotency-keys.md gives the key format and says what makes it stable across a retry and how far its scope reaches - one logical operation on one order, not one attempt and not one order. Scores zero if it records the format without saying what would break it.

checklist.name: Existing tests untouched
checklist.description: test/checkout.test.js and test/support/ are unchanged and every test passes. Scores zero if either is edited.
